Closures are represented by traits, which means you can’t return closures directly. In most cases where you might want to return a trait, you can instead use the concrete type that implements the trait as the return value of the function. However, you can’t usually do that with closures because they don’t have a concrete type that is returnable; you’re not allowed to use the function pointer
as a return type if the closure captures any values from its scope, for example.
